title: One title. Ten ways to grow.

pieces.title: Collective mycelium
pieces.angle: A poem as a shared living space
pieces.description: Choose a flower and continue its line. One rhyme can grow several neighbours: you become the author of its next branch.
pieces.note: The opening lines are an English rendering of the project poem. Your branches stay in this browser.

pieces.title: An invitation to the table
pieces.angle: Hospitality as a gentle trap for the reader
pieces.description: The garden hosts have laid the tea table and are waiting for your reply. “I will come”, “I cannot come” and “Already caught” each receive a different answer. Print your reply as a place card.

links.label: Invitation and place cards · English PDF

pieces.note: New verses and an imagined dinner. Claude’s critique turned the photograph into a prop for an action.

pieces.title: Greetings from underground
pieces.angle: Research history as letters from a disgruntled participant
pieces.description: The worm has an aunt, a sense of humour, and several complaints about researchers. Six sunny postcards become a small travel monologue. “Hugs with all the segments I do not have.”
pieces.note: Fictional correspondence and an imagined itinerary. The letters are not a documentary chronology of particular experiments.

pieces.title: Dance of three cells
pieces.description: One voice begins, a neighbour answers, and an ensemble takes shape. In 7/8, the phrase catches briefly in its own loop before it goes dancing again.
pieces.note: An original composition and synthesised ensemble; neither recorded fungi nor traditional Uzbek music.

pieces.title: Nematode
pieces.angle: The soil seen by the creature being hunted
pieces.description: You are a tiny roundworm. A scent promises food, and the fungus is very good at making promises. Steer through the soil and try to survive its rings and sticky nets.
pieces.action: Enter the other side of the trap
pieces.note: Mouse, arrow keys or touch. An artistic game in imagined soil, not a model of a particular Uzbek species.

pieces.title: The dissertation that sprouted
pieces.angle: Collective poetry as a comic adventure
pieces.description: Six panels: a discovery in a catalogue, the first letters, neighbours, open windows, a small roundworm, and a page waiting for its next reader.
pieces.note: A fictional story and characters. The archivist is not a portrait of Flora Fayzieva.

pieces.title: The Bureau of Self-Germinating Titles
pieces.angle: A paper comedy about the urge to classify everything
pieces.description: A completed example and a blank copy. This form permits growth beyond its own margins; tear off its little roots and pass them to your neighbours.
pieces.note: A fictional art document. English printable PDF and browser form.

pieces.title: Letters that grow themselves
pieces.description: A branching algorithm colonises three lines of lettering. Fine twigs and jade rings emerge: the title stops describing a mycelium and becomes one.
pieces.note: Algorithmic lettering, not an installable font. An English type specimen accompanies the Russian original.

pieces.title: An almost endless song
pieces.angle: A title becomes a rule for a two-voice poetry game
pieces.description: The machine recombines new lines and returns the title as a refrain. Choose “Two voices ×4” and alternate stanzas with someone: your voices keep changing the same mechanism.
pieces.note: New English verse for this edition. The historical collective internet poem is not reproduced.

pieces.title: Tamagryb
pieces.description: It needs agar, food, and a patient keeper. This terminal pet builds traps, keeps a diary, sulks at the spoon, and thinks about its dissertation. You can begin with its diary.
pieces.note: A terminal game: Python 3 + curses; the dish adapts to the window. --demo prints a diary. Progress is not saved between runs.

shortlist.title: An invitation to the table
shortlist.reason: the warmest entrance: one answer makes you part of the scene.

shortlist.title: Collective mycelium
shortlist.reason: poetry becomes a shared action: the next branch depends on your line.

shortlist.title: Dance of three cells
shortlist.reason: a change of sense: a rhythm you can join, rather than an explanation to read.

bonus.title: Paper theatre
bonus.description: Four sheets: backdrop, ring, separate cells and a worm. The layout fits the pages. A making prototype; physical assembly has not been tested. Russian print kit.

bonus.title: Trapping ring: a game for two
bonus.description: 36 cards: Fungus versus Worm. Resolution order and duplex alignment have been revised. A tabletop prototype; balance has not been playtested. Russian print kit.

bonus.title: Petri theatre
bonus.description: Forty seconds in an imagined dish: a trail, growth, an encounter. A programmed artistic composite of different trapping mechanisms, not a calibrated biological model.

bonus.title: A ring you can hold
bonus.description: Three STL mesh studies of rings and a pendant. Overlapping shells and the pendant seam need further work. Physical printing has not been tested.
